newsitem.title: USA: New airline terminal possible at Cleveland airport.
newsitem.headline: New airline terminal possible at Cleveland airport.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc may be eyeing a new terminal at Cleveland Hopkins International Airport, according to a report in the Cleveland Plain Dealer.
However, spokespersons for both the airline and the airport declined on Wednesday to directly address if talks were underway for a terminal.

A Continental spokeswoman verified comments in the report by airline chairman Gordon Bethune that the airline's spending would focus this year on Cleveland with new jet-powered commuter planes and that the airline was looking at some airport improvements that would utilize more of those planes.
Mark Butler, an airport spokesman, said Continental and other airlines had approached the airport in the past six months to talk about projects.
Meanwhile, negotiations are continuing between Cleveland and Brook Park over a runway project that is part of a $500 million, five-year airport expansion project, Butler said.

A tentative agreement between the mayors of the two municipalities was announced in August. An airport official has said the runway project would be financed with general airport revenue bonds and federal aviation grant funds.
